SL-000042.transcript:
Member (Mei Kim): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Mei Kim, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Kim): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Mei Kim): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Mei Kim): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Mei Kim): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Mei Kim): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Mei Kim): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Mei Kim): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Mei Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The first request was missing the radiograph date. The second one is complete and has been assessed, and it's approved. Your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Mei Kim): So the crown is covered now?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Yes. It's approved at your plan's coverage level, and your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Mei Kim): Do I pay anything?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: the crown is approved, and your dentist will get the confirmation today with your co-payment.
Member (Mei Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent Kevin Nguyen reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 5 (very satisfied).

Member (Gurpreet Martin): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Gurpreet Martin, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Martin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Gurpreet Martin): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Gurpreet Martin): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which pharmacy are you using?
Member (Gurpreet Martin): The one near my work. They said they can resubmit as soon as it's approved.

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

SL-000090.transcript:
Member (Tyler Singh): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Tyler Singh, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Singh): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Singh): Yes, that's right.
Member (Tyler Singh): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Tyler Singh): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Tyler Singh): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Tyler Singh): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Tyler Singh): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Tyler Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Tyler Singh): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Tyler Singh): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Tyler Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Tyler Martin): I cancelled my life insurance before it renewed and you still took the payment.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Tyler Martin, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Yes, the full amount. The refund request is approved and goes back to the same account.
Member (Tyler Martin): Will I get something in writing?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Yes, a cancellation confirmation by mail within ten days.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the policy is cancelled, the 750 dollars is on its way back, and a written confirmation will follow.
Member (Tyler Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Liam Martin): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Liam Martin, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Martin): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Liam Martin): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Liam Martin): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Liam Martin): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Liam Martin): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Liam Martin): They said they called and got the same answer as me.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Liam Martin): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Liam Martin): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Liam Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Noah O'Brien, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah O'Brien): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Noah O'Brien): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Noah O'Brien): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Noah O'Brien): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Noah O'Brien): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000284.transcript:
Member (Owen Chen): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Owen Chen, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Chen): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Chen): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Owen Chen): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Owen Chen): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Owen Chen): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Owen Chen): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Owen Chen): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Owen Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Owen Chen): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Owen Chen): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Owen Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000376.transcript:
Member (Mei Kim): My life insurance premium tripled and nobody warned me.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Mei Kim, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Kim): It went from about 250 to 750 dollars a month.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Kim): I called two weeks before the renewal date to cancel.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which policy is this about?
Member (Mei Kim): My term life policy. It renewed this month.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Is the payment still coming from the same bank account?
Member (Mei Kim): Yes, same account.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): If the cost came down, would you want to keep some coverage?
Member (Mei Kim): Maybe, if it's affordable.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the policy billing history and the forms received.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I can see your call from the 17th and the renewal payment taken on the 1st.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The renewal rate is higher because the policy moved into a new age band on renewal.
Member (Mei Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Mei Kim): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The premium increase follows the renewal schedule in your policy, so I can't change the rate. I can send you the renewal notice and your options, including reducing the coverage amount.
Member (Mei Kim): Nobody told me it would triple.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The notice went out 60 days before renewal, but I understand it's a shock at that size.
Member (Mei Kim): How much would a lower amount cost?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Halving the coverage brings it to about 375 dollars a month. The comparison I'm sending shows a few options.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Mei Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Gurpreet Kim, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Who follows up?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Member (Liam Campbell): I cancelled my life insurance before it renewed and you still took the payment.

Member (Liam Campbell): How much would a lower amount cost?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Halving the coverage brings it to about 375 dollars a month. The comparison I'm sending shows a few options.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the new rate follows the renewal schedule, I've sent you the notice and a lower-coverage option, and you can decide within 30 days.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): No, all future claims will go to the new one.

Member (Tyler Ahmed): I'm following up again — my dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Tyler Ahmed, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Ahmed): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Tyler Ahmed): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Tyler Ahmed): Yes, that's right.
Member (Tyler Ahmed): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Tyler Ahmed): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Tyler Ahmed): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has the dental office called us about this directly?

Member (Tyler Ahmed): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Tyler Ahmed): What should my dentist include this time?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
